title: Reading List
content:
[32606 Database | Reading List]
Recommended pre-reading for 32606 Database

- Michael Mannino, Database Application Development.
- ISBN: 0072463678.

This text is recommended as background reading for students who want to become familiar with database concepts and database application development before or during the subject.

title: Assignments – Assessment Overview
content:

Assessments in 32606 Database.

Assessment 1: SQL Test 1
- Due: 4 September 2026 at 14:00
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- In-class SQL test. Students write SQL statements and submit their SQL code together with the output produced by the queries.

Assessment 2: SQL Test 2
- Due: 11 September 2026 at 14:00
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- A second in-class SQL test focusing on more advanced SQL skills.

Assessment 3: ACID Properties and Integrity Constraints
- Due: 15 September 2026 at 11:11
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- Short written responses on entity, domain and referential integrity, ACID properties, and an ERD task based on a supplied scenario.

Assessment 4: ERD Task
- Due: 29 September 2026 at 11:11
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- Students draw an entity-relationship diagram from a supplied database scenario and identify the required relationships accurately.

Assessment 5: Database Project
- Due: 5 October 2026 at 23:59
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- Students design and build a small database project based on a self-selected real-world problem, develop an ERD, and obtain feedback on the proposed design.

title: Assessment 1 - SQL Test 1
content:
[32606 Database | Assessment 1 - SQL Test 1]
Assessment 1 is an in-class SQL test conducted during the scheduled lab. Students receive the questions in class and write SQL statements to obtain the required results.

- The test contains approximately 3-4 SQL questions.
- Students have about 50 minutes to complete the SQL work.
- For each question, students should write the SQL statement and check the output.
- Students then copy their SQL code and query output and submit them through the Canvas assignment page.
- Students must attend the scheduled lab to receive and complete the test.
